narrative.overview: The page is a silkscreened festival poster that happens to work: Buenaventura billed like a music festival of the Pacific, with the humpback whale as the headliner. Every section is a full field of one flat ink, and type is set the way a poster printer sets a bill: compressed, heavy, uppercase, stacked tight. Depth comes from print, not from screens: half-tone, misregistration, two-ink duotones, the turbante border strip and rubber stamps.
keyCharacteristics: Flat ink fields own whole sections; no gradients on surfaces.
Anybody at narrow widths (52–80 %) for every display voice; Figtree for reading.
Print devices with a job: half-tone for shading, duotone for photos, stamps for saved state, a border strip between bands.
Floating panels ("volantes") are paper handbills that can be dragged and tilt with velocity.

rules.name: The Full Field Rule
rules.body: An ink is either a whole section ground or a functional mark (chip, button, stamp, line). Never a scattered accent on a neutral page.

rules.name: The Tinted Secondary Rule
rules.body: Secondary text is tinted from its own field, never a neutral gray.

rules.name: The Numbers in Ink Rule
rules.body: Live values are set in the display face with tabular figures; their labels stay small in Figtree.

rules.name: The No Kicker Rule
rules.body: No small label above a heading. Context lines go under the title.

rules.name: The Misregistration Rule
rules.body: The only offset second color is a print plate under display type (0.016em), and it registers to zero on hover. It is never a box shadow.

dos: Do give every new section one full ink field from the five-ink palette.
Do set titles in Anybody at 52–72 % width, uppercase, with the context line underneath.
Do reprint photographs as two-ink duotones with the half-tone overlay, and show the true color on hover or in detail views.
Do mark saved or chosen things with the stamp, not a color swap alone.
Do use the turbante strip only between major bands.
donts: Don't put a kicker or small label above a heading.
Don't use gradients, glass or blur as decoration on surfaces.
Don't use hard zero-blur box shadows; the only offset color is the registration plate under display type.
Don't use gray for secondary text; tint it from the field.
Don't use emoji or glyphs as icons; icons are Lucide at 2.2–2.6 stroke.
